\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়} (ghūrnijhôṛ)}{ঘূর্ণিঝড় (ghūrnijhôṛ)}]{\bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়} (ghūrnijhôṛ) — a cyclone}

\label{lesson:BN-C288-ghurnijhor}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for at once, then the Bengali for to crash down.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়}}
\textbf{\bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়}} — \emph{ghūrnijhôṛ} — \textquotedblleft{}a cyclone\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{সমুদ্র} \bn{থেকে} \bn{একটা} \bn{বড়} \bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়} \bn{আসছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{sômudrô theke ekṭā bôṛo ghūrnijhôṛ āschhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
A big cyclone was coming in from the sea.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়}} (\emph{ghūrnijhôṛ}) joins Sanskrit \emph{ghūrṇi}, 'a whirling' (Monier-Williams), to \textbf{\bn{ঝড়}}, a storm: a whirling storm.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghūrnijhôṛ}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghūrnijhôṛ}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{sômudrô theke ekṭā bôṛo ghūrnijhôṛ āschhilô.} — A big cyclone was coming in from the sea.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for at once, then the Bengali for to crash down, then say \emph{ghūrnijhôṛ} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A cyclone\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উপকূল} (upôkūl)}{উপকূল (upôkūl)}]{\bn{উপকূল} (upôkūl) — a coast}

\label{lesson:BN-C288-upokul}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to crash down, then the Bengali for a cyclone.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উপকূল}}
\textbf{\bn{উপকূল}} — \emph{upôkūl} — \textquotedblleft{}a coast\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঘূর্ণিঝড়ের} \bn{আগে} \bn{উপকূলের} \bn{মানুষ} \bn{গ্রাম} \bn{ছেড়ে} \bn{চলে} \bn{গেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{ghūrnijhôṛer āge upôkūler mānush grām chheṛe chôle gelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
Before the cyclone the people of the coast left their villages.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উপকূল}} (\emph{upôkūl}) is Sanskrit \emph{upakūla}, 'being on the shore' (Monier-Williams): \emph{upa-}, 'near', and \emph{kūla}, 'a bank'.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upôkūl}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upôkūl}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{ghūrnijhôṛer āge upôkūler mānush grām chheṛe chôle gelô.} — Before the cyclone the people of the coast left their villages.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to crash down, then the Bengali for a cyclone, then say \emph{upôkūl} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উপকূল} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}A coast\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{এগোনো} (egono)}{এগোনো (egono)}]{\bn{এগোনো} (egono) — to move forward; to advance}

\label{lesson:BN-C288-egono}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a cyclone, then the Bengali for a coast.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{এগোনো}}
\textbf{\bn{এগোনো}} — \emph{egono} — \textquotedblleft{}to move forward; to advance\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঝড়টা} \bn{ধীরে} \bn{ধীরে} \bn{উপকূলের} \bn{দিকে} \bn{এগোচ্ছিল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jhôṛṭā dhīre dhīre upôkūler dike egochchhilô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The storm was slowly moving towards the coast.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{ঝড়} \bn{এগোল}, \emph{sei jhôṛ egolô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{এগোনো}} (\emph{egono}) is usually explained as built on \textbf{\bn{আগে}}, in front — Sanskrit \emph{agra}, 'top, front' (CDIAL 68) — with the verb ending: to go to the front, to move forward.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{egono}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{egono}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhôṛṭā dhīre dhīre upôkūler dike egochchhilô.} — The storm was slowly moving towards the coast.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a cyclone, then the Bengali for a coast, then say \emph{egono} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{এগোনো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To move forward; to advance\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.

\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{উপড়ানো} (upṛāno)}{উপড়ানো (upṛāno)}]{\bn{উপড়ানো} (upṛāno) — to uproot}

\label{lesson:BN-C288-uprano}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for a coast, then the Bengali for to move forward.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{উপড়ানো}}
\textbf{\bn{উপড়ানো}} — \emph{upṛāno} — \textquotedblleft{}to uproot\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঝড়ে} \bn{রাস্তার} \bn{অনেক} \bn{গাছ} \bn{উপড়ে} \bn{গেল।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jhôṛe rāstār ônek gāchh upṛe gelô.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
The storm uprooted many trees along the road.
\end{quote}

Past (he/she …): \bn{সেই} \bn{ঝড়} \bn{গাছটা} \bn{উপড়াল}, \emph{sei jhôṛ gāchhṭā upṛālô}.

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{উপড়ানো}} (\emph{upṛāno}) comes down from Sanskrit \emph{utpāṭayati}, 'roots up', and its partner \emph{utpaṭati}, 'bursts open' (CDIAL 1809, which lists Bengali \emph{upaṛā}, 'to come up by the roots').
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upṛāno}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{upṛāno}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhôṛe rāstār ônek gāchh upṛe gelô.} — The storm uprooted many trees along the road.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for a coast, then the Bengali for to move forward, then say \emph{upṛāno} again
\end{itemize}

\begin{tcolorbox}[breakable,colback=teal!4,colframe=teal!35!black,title={Before you move on}]
What does \bn{উপড়ানো} mean? (\textquotedblleft{}To uproot\textquotedblright{}.) Say it once more.
\end{tcolorbox}
\section[\texorpdfstring{\bn{বিদ্যুৎ} (bidyut)}{বিদ্যুৎ (bidyut)}]{\bn{বিদ্যুৎ} (bidyut) — electricity; lightning}

\label{lesson:BN-C288-bidyut}



\begin{quote}
Before the new one: say the Bengali for to move forward, then the Bengali for to uproot.
\end{quote}

\subsection*{You'll want to know: \bn{বিদ্যুৎ}}
\textbf{\bn{বিদ্যুৎ}} — \emph{bidyut} — \textquotedblleft{}electricity; lightning\textquotedblright{}.

\begin{quote}
\bn{ঝড়ের} \bn{রাতে} \bn{গ্রামে} \bn{বিদ্যুৎ} \bn{ছিল} \bn{না।}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
\emph{jhôṛer rāte grāme bidyut chhilô nā.}
\end{quote}

\begin{quote}
There was no electricity in the village on the night of the storm.
\end{quote}

\begin{cousinweb}
\textbf{\bn{বিদ্যুৎ}} (\emph{bidyut}) is Sanskrit \emph{vidyut}, lightning, from \emph{vi-√dyut}, 'to flash forth' (Monier-Williams). Bengali uses it for lightning and for the power in the wires.
\end{cousinweb}

\begin{grammarlens}[title={What you've built}]
One more word for telling what happened.
\end{grammarlens}

\subsection*{Your turn}
\begin{itemize}
\raggedright
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bidyut}
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{bidyut}, once more
  \item \emph{Say it:} \emph{jhôṛer rāte grāme bidyut chhilô nā.} — There was no electricity in the village on the night of the storm.
  \item \emph{Recall:} say the Bengali for to move forward, then the Bengali for to uproot, then say \emph{bidyut} again
\end{itemize}
